texto: I can understand why this movie was ground breaking when it released. I can also understand why many people still enjoy it. However… this movie is one big existentialist acid trip with required reading and a message that really falls flat for about 73% of the film. The remaining 27% is the only bit of the movie where anything interesting happens that an average movie enjoyer is able to follow. All of the bits with HAL and the astronauts are solid. There’s a reason why HAL’s iconic lines are still quoted to this day. But if you had asked me to predict what the first twenty minutes of this would be before watching it, “a whole lotta nothing with some monkeys” would not have been my guess… but here we are.

texto: Visually, this is beautiful. The set pieces, costumes, and spaceship designs all look magnificent, especially for the 60s. Nevertheless, this movie is indeed a snooze fest. Yes, I understand that the movie was intentionally made this way, with a lack of dialogue, and that the story was meant to be told through visual effects and sound. But that doesn’t mean it’s not boring as all hell. I genuinely think people who are calling this a masterpiece or giving it super high ratings are just trying to be different. Just because the movie was made to be told this way doesn’t automatically make it good. The visuals and set pieces do not carry this movie enough for me to care about it at all. Compared to the other two Kubrick movies I’ve watched, this is abysmal.

texto: I got in a debate with my mate the other day about the best directors of all time. He made a good point about Stanley Kubrick and the influence he has had on cinema. I have already watched some Stanley Kubrick, notable Full Metal Jacket which I thought was incredible, so I decided to check out more of his work and watch 2001 - A Space Odyssey. What stood out was the visual and practical affects. For a film close to 60 years old, I was definitely surprised by every shot. I liked the use of the rotating cameras while in the spaceships that created a futuristic sense, and can only imagine what that would've felt like to see in cinema when it released. I have to say Kubrick is very creative in this aspect, but the film fell off because of the story and the pacing. It felt like Kubrick was just throwing things into the film because he wanted to, not because they had significant meaning that added to the story. As well as this, I feel like much more emotion could've been portrayed, such as when HAL was being shut down, Dave hardly showed any emotion and was almost as robotic as the computer, which may have been done on purpose, but this choice doesn't have any weight when we don't know his character and personality anyway. Overall this film could have been a lot better, mainly through the story and pacing, which leads me to the conclusion that it is a bit overrated, and seems to be over hyped just because it's a Stanley Kubrick film.

texto: My whole review went away twice due to my phone just crashing wtf… trying again now hopefully (on my laptop). Aw man I really don’t know where to begin and usually that isn’t a good sign. I really wanted to love this Kubrick ‘masterpiece’ but it just let me down noo.. I’ll just answer all the questions I got. Is it beautiful? Yes of course, how he went from dr. Strangelove to this within 4 years is beyond me. I can’t deny every scene looks amazing, even if this would come out today it would still be visually stunning. Hell, it even looks better than Star Wars coming out ten years later. I can understand that this was the coolest thing back in the 60's. Are the characters interesting? No, and I don't think they're meant to. The only interesting character is the onboard computer Hal. His whole sequence is the only intriguing part about the whole film, he really carried. How is the story telling? It grabs a very big time period, with big jumps in time for sure, but still pretty interesting. Seeing how an unidentifiable object started our 'smart' human evolution. And is still ruling us millions of years later on. But it is slow and lacks so much explanation. They really tell very little, meant so okay, but the beauty shots in replacement don't do the job enough to keep you engaged. Is it boring? Yes, unfortunately it is. The first act is cool and funny with the monkeys, hiring real people to play in a monkey-costume works really well, but it took a bit too long. The second act about the voyage to the moon is just out and out boring. The third act with Hal, is as said the only really interesting sequence of the whole movie. The end is just confusing and so weird to be fair. Some scenes are very beautiful yes, but taking soo long for fk sake. That really drained me, why do they need to take soo long, pretty boring. Do the themes work? So So. Aliens are fascinating of course, and the idea of another society secretly controlling ours is intriguing. I really liked that realisation came on very late, that was smart and adds to the story for sure, but there was very little explanation, missed chance in my opinion. Is there a final plus? Yes for crying out loud, the score in this film is impeccable! It is the only thing keeping the space shots bearable, but still they take so long even the music can't carry to keep you invested anymore. I think I’m just a bit frustrated. I believe anyone hyping up this movie has to be watching this through their 60's glasses. For then this would be incredible, but now this is just a snoozefest for too much of the film. I'm mostly just dissapointed it didn't live up to the high everyone was talking about. I waited until I would have time to watch this and be invested for it, but it still took me two days/sessions to finish this, because the 20-60 minute timeframe is soo long and boring. All with all, yes I would be open to watch this in a theatre, I think the visuals would definitely win me over more, together with the loud music it could for sure change my opinion in a good way. But for now on a TV it was just not interesting enough. Thanks Hal for carrying somewhat, for god's sake. 3*

texto: I hate that I didn’t like this the first time I saw it. I hate that I disliked it again this time around.  I hated the very ambiguous everything. I hated the 10 minute long takes of a ship in space. And I hated that I hated it because I love Kubrick! This time around I definitely appreciated the cinematography more. But why, why does it have to be so drawn out? I don’t need 2 minutes of black screen for the opening part of the film. Now, to praise some shots: I love the window shots, something is always moving. And how did he film the leopard scene? That was crazy. Other than that though, I thought Kubrick was just flexing what he can do with a camera. The shots are just overdone for my taste. Was the cinematography good? Yes. Was the villain semi decent? Yes! Is this my least favorite Kubrick? YES! Maybe I just don’t get it. But I really just don’t think it’s for me. Still getting the box set though. Edit: I feel like I mostly hated on it in this review so I wanted to come back and say that some of my favorite films as a kid, Star Wars, would not be made along with many others had it not been for this film. And it is a masterfully well-crafted piece of art. Probably some of Kubrick’s best. But it’s not as well-rounded as I find most of his others to be.

I have already watched some Stanley Kubrick, notable Full Metal Jacket which I thought was incredible, so I decided to check out more of his work and watch 2001 - A Space Odyssey. I liked the use of the rotating cameras while in the spaceships that created a futuristic sense, and can only imagine what that would've felt like to see in cinema when it released. texto: Visionnaire, mais chiant. Une image et visuels incroyable. Que ce soit dans la composition, dans les couleurs, ou même encore les designs des environnements. Le film à une esthétique bien propre à lui, et surtout ptn, 1968, et les effets spéciaux sont bluffant pour l'époque. Je comprend qu'il soit considéré comme un classique révolutionnaire. C'est assez marrant de voir que la communication entre homme et machine soit un tel fantasme à l'époque, aujourd'hui en 2026 avec le prime de l'ia, c'est plus du tout étonnant de communiquer et pouvoir discuter avec une machine. En tout cas, je valide aussi le coté visionnaire, le conflit entre IA et humains etc. On est en pleins dedans lol. Une musique mythique, un classique indéniable, mais une lenteur abyssale ptn A la moitié du film ya eu une entracte, j'arrivais pas à me dire qu'il restait encore 1h15 (ressenti 3h), et frr chaque action prends 20min, c une dinguerie. Mais j'ai tout de même adoré les longs dialogues entre HAL et Dave, et de voir comment ils s'imaginaient le concept d'intelligence artificielle supreme et superieur à tous. ah oui et les singes sont super bien faits

texto: I hate that I didn’t like this the first time I saw it. I hate that I disliked it again this time around.  I hated the very ambiguous everything. I hated the 10 minute long takes of a ship in space. And I hated that I hated it because I love Kubrick! This time around I definitely appreciated the cinematography more. But why, why does it have to be so drawn out? I don’t need 2 minutes of black screen for the opening part of the film. Now, to praise some shots: I love the window shots, something is always moving. And how did he film the leopard scene? That was crazy. Other than that though, I thought Kubrick was just flexing what he can do with a camera. The shots are just overdone for my taste. Was the cinematography good? Yes. Was the villain semi decent? Yes! Is this my least favorite Kubrick? YES! Maybe I just don’t get it. But I really just don’t think it’s for me. Still getting the box set though. Edit: I feel like I mostly hated on it in this review so I wanted to come back and say that some of my favorite films as a kid, Star Wars, would not be made along with many others had it not been for this film. And it is a masterfully well-crafted piece of art. Probably some of Kubrick’s best. But it’s not as well-rounded as I find most of his others to be.

texto: As much as I love Kubrick and as much as this is probably the most technically impressive film ever, there’s only so much jerking off to one’s own cinematography that I can take. And I love Barry Lyndon (which I often hear being called boring and style-over-substance by critics), but I think it’s got a super compelling narrative and cast; that film is infinitely more of an ‘odyssey’ than 2001: A Space Odyssey is. What is Kubrick actually trying to say in this? People will say this film explores themes like human evolution and our place in the universe, but it has very little to actually say about it. We watch all these glorious sequences of evolution and vast expanses in space, but what is the point ? I don’t dislike films with unconvential narratives and very little character focus, as long as they are being used to communicate something. But there is very little point to this film other than for Kubrick to revel in his undeniable technical prowess. Boy, I can’t wait to watch Solaris now…

texto: I got in a debate with my mate the other day about the best directors of all time. He made a good point about Stanley Kubrick and the influence he has had on cinema. I have already watched some Stanley Kubrick, notable Full Metal Jacket which I thought was incredible, so I decided to check out more of his work and watch 2001 - A Space Odyssey. What stood out was the visual and practical affects. For a film close to 60 years old, I was definitely surprised by every shot. I liked the use of the rotating cameras while in the spaceships that created a futuristic sense, and can only imagine what that would've felt like to see in cinema when it released. I have to say Kubrick is very creative in this aspect, but the film fell off because of the story and the pacing. It felt like Kubrick was just throwing things into the film because he wanted to, not because they had significant meaning that added to the story. As well as this, I feel like much more emotion could've been portrayed, such as when HAL was being shut down, Dave hardly showed any emotion and was almost as robotic as the computer, which may have been done on purpose, but this choice doesn't have any weight when we don't know his character and personality anyway. Overall this film could have been a lot better, mainly through the story and pacing, which leads me to the conclusion that it is a bit overrated, and seems to be over hyped just because it's a Stanley Kubrick film.

texto: Every watch is just more fully appreciating how this movie’s DNA is scattered through any movie about space made ever since. It’s wild how singular the vision for every single little detail in this movie is before we had even been to the moon, and how all of the beautifully rendered and dynamic CGI of Interstellar, or even the ambitious and groundbreaking VFX of Star Wars pales in comparison to a matte painting and a rotating miniature with unidirectional lighting when composed just right, with the proper intention and ambience. Same with the BCU of Hal’s red dot, same with all the monolith shots and the dawn of man looking better than the best nature documentary. 2001 is the monolith Kubrick sent us from the future to teach us a new form of art we weren’t ready for yet and still aren’t for the most part.

texto: The last time I watched this movie, I was much younger and wrote "maybe I'll have a different opinion when I watch it again" — I gave it one star more. I truly think this is an extraordinary achievement in filmmaking for it's time, but I also think that's the same thing that hurts it. The desire to show the genius-innovations of shots makes it feel less like a film, and more like a cinematographer's demo reel. I think in this age of AI, this plot is very much relevant; so I would argue the film still is important today. It definitely deserves respect for the impact it had on filmmaking as a whole. But as much as it's uncomfortable to go against the grain on a Kubrick film review, I believe there is a difference between an "impressive" film and an "enjoyable" one. And without the latter half, it falls short from being a "great" one.

texto: Recent 4k Blu-ray rewatch. A masterpiece and visual spectacle that is a little bit too self aware of its own weight. Do stunning visuals alone make for a fun movie? Absolutely not. You need to be in the mood for this. Preferably in a dark room. I still say to myself, how the fuck does a movie from 1968 look this good?? Beyond that.. from a pace and storytelling standpoint, it falls apart a bit. Frustrating pacing and disjointed at times. I love it. But I don’t need to see it again for another 15 years.

texto: Vu au cinéma pour la première fois alors forcément ça en jette ! Regarder ça en 2026 alors que le film date de 1968 reste toujours extraordinaire pour moi ! Genre KUBRICK sortait ce film alors que l’Homme n’avait pas encore mis un pied sur la Lune ! C’est fou. Et c’est là où je trouves ce film exceptionnel, c’est tellement novateur et visionnaire. Les effets spéciaux sont impressionnants pour l’époque c’est complètement fou ! Cependant, le gros gros défaut c’est le rythme malheureusement. Le film souffre d’énormes longueurs. Honnêtement y’a des séquences qu’ont subies parfois tellement c’est long. De plus, la compréhension du récit est un peu hasardeuse. Y’a aucun problème à ne pas tout saisir à un film mais là ça semble vraiment confus (selon moi). En tout cas je ne peux pas mettre moins de 3 étoiles car le statut de chef d’œuvre est mérité ! Je pense que tous les films d’espace sont passé par 2001 tellement ça a posé les bases avant quiconque  !

texto: littéralement la définition d’une prouesse technique. la mise en scène est absolument dingue, les effets spéciaux sont à l’image de cette prouesse, notamment la représentation de l’espace qui est juste folle, tout le long du film on se retrouve emportés dans une expérience visuelle hallucinante avec des images magnifiques. L’odyssée De L’espace reste malgré tout lent dans sa construction et son rythme ce qui dérange logiquement une grande partie du public mais lorsque qu’on s’immerge vraiment dans le film, cette lenteur ne semble pas du tout pesante et devient même agréable puisqu’elle permet de réellement entrer dans cette expérience en profitant des images splendides . pour revenir sur la mise en scène, les plans sont d’une beauté folle et il ne faut évidemment pas oublier les mouvements de caméra hypnotisants qui nous font réellement ressentir la pesanteur de la station, j’ai aussi beaucoup apprécié la très bonne gestion du silence accentuant la tension omniprésente, on peut évidemment aborder le sujet des musiques qui sont aujourd’hui iconiques et qui nous marquent lors du premier visionnage par leur sensation de donner aux images cet aspect toujours plus grandiose. durant tout le film Stanley Kubrick prend le temps de nous montrer les choses sans pour autant nous les expliquer nous laissant dans le flou et dans le trouble, notamment avec sa fin marquante, je suis amoureux de ce que produit cet homme. en bref, pour un film de 1968 il n’a absolument pas mal vieilli, au contraire vu le contexte actuel avec l’IA etc qui peut remettre en question cette légitimité dans son utilisation, c’est sans aucun doute l’un des plus grands films de tous les temps, ma review est même pas à la hauteur de ce chef d’œuvre.

texto: Like if Harry met Sally but there's no Sally and Harry was kind of a loser. Really that's the main bone I have to pick with this — the guy kinda sucks and everything revolves around him. His loser friends, his faux-precocious younger sister, his boss, his co-workers, and most importantly, Summer, all orbit him and have seemingly no life of their own. Every word they say or action they take is a reaction to Tom's behaviour — or if it isn't it goes brazenly unexplained. Why is Summer so commitment-shy and avoidant? There must be some thing there, some semblance of personal history that we're just not getting a god damn hint of. She tells him of her past boyfriends (played for laughs), she cries at the ending of the graduate (getting there, but you still end up asking why ?), and that's as close as we get to seeing who she is as a person. As an individual. The other thing though is that I don't mind some of what's done here. I laughed out loud a few times at the beginning — there really is some fun to be had, especially when the interests of the main guy are tailored almost a little too specifically to yours. But fuckin' christ Marc Webb, really? Summer's basically a cardboard cutout for your fantasies to get sketched onto, dude. She's not exactly manic, nor very pixie — and even though she is girl (Zooeyy Deschanelll! He llo!) she's mostly dream. The character trait of adamantly defending Ringo Starr as her favourite beatle is some shit I'd come up with in 20 minutes on a throwaway daydream, dude, like c'mon. Put me in a boring two hour lecture and I could whip up some wayyy better shit. Some shit that puts a dumb ass smile on my face. But that's not the point the point is that I'm also kind of a loser and when I put on a rom-com I don't want to see some shit I can outclass in a daydream I want to see real people (♪ and I want to see [real] liiife ♪) that are grounded in their own unique lived experiences and who share their thoughts and opinions and feelings between each other — I want to see people with flaws that are given reason to, I want to see people who both act and react in equal amounts. Or at least I want to see Nora Ephron's name on the writing credits, cause otherwise the com isn't gonna cover up for the rom. Speakin' of the com, which I said I kinda liked before, it actually kinda sucks balls. A lot of it's referential. And that's okay, y'know. But it's just a little too referential. Like you're standing on the shoulders of giants and you feel the need to point that out, and not only point it out but make pointing it out be a large part of what you're bringing to the table? You don't need to be giant, of course, but when you can't be bothered to try and make something feel big or original in your own movie — that's when the nods start to grate on me. I will say the ending is actually really cute but I'm staying strong on this rating. I kept wanting it to be over the longer it went on, and while I'd like to say it was neither here nor there, it leaned towards the there just that tiny, unjustifiable bit more. I mean, fuck me. That Thomas fuckin' Hansen of all guys has to be the poster boy for The Smiths in the modern zeitgeist is nothing short of a tragedy. All that being said, if thirteen year-old me had ever gotten my hands on this I would have fallen completely and absolutely head over heels. What that spells out for the quality of the film, well... take that as you will. Also who's gonna tell him there's only like 365 days in a year what the fuck do you mean 500 days of summer that's like astronomically impossible.

texto: I was angry so I decided to watch this movie and now I’m angry about this movie. Like, it’s a good movie, but Summer drives me up the wall! She is totally valid in wanting a casual relationship, but it is so obvious Tom has other ideas and she is only making things worse by continuing the relationship. In what situation are those two “just friends”? I’d be mad, too! I don’t know where Summer got the idea they were “just friends” after specifically saying they were in a “casual relationship”. Overall, they both had problems defining the relationship: Tom wanted more and misread signs; Summer acted hot and cold and gave out confusing signals. I ranted for about two more paragraphs, but I decided I looked insane so I deleted them. So, all of this to say, I don’t like Summer, Tom is fine, this movie is good in theory but I HATE it, I’m so angry, I wish I never watched this movie, and I should just rewatch 10 Things I Hate About You. (However, on rewatching it, I’m not as angry as I was before. I hate Summer more, and I hate Tom less, and I overall hate this movie).

texto: A ver en justificación no tan justificable de Summer, ella avisó que esto era casual, que no quería un novio y que no creía en el amor ni nada, pero lo que no me parece es el hecho de que haya llamado en un momento a esa relación como una “amistad” siendo que efectivamente (dándole la razón a Tom) los amigos no se tratan ni deberían tratarse así (como relación). También siento que lo ilusionó a Tom pero recalcando siempre que no iba a llegar a nada. Después hablando del hecho de que ella nunca haya encontrado lo que buscaba y le “llenaba” en Tom, no la hace culpable ni mala persona, es algo actualmente real que ha pasado, está pasando o pasará en cualquiera de nosotros. Simplemente más tarde encontró a alguien que sí le dio lo que ella buscaba y era lo que quería tan así que decidió casarse. Y de la parte de Tom, lo que creo es que se aferró a la idea de que Summer era el amor de su vida y que sería su “alma gemela”, sabiendo aún e ignorando lo que ella le había aclarado desde un inicio, en pocas palabras se ilusionó y la idealizó demasiado solo por compartir mismos gustos y rarezas. Además tomó como “destino” el cruzarse en el trabajo con ella porque efectivamente eran compañeros y a él, ella solo le atraía físicamente. Él tenía las expectativas de en sueño con ella, cuando ella siempre le demostraba en la cara que eso no era así, pero él cegado con su idealización. Fin

texto: Rewatched this for probably the tenth time and it still gets me in a completely different way each time depending on where I am in life. It's such a sharp, unsentimental look at how we construct narratives around people — Tom isn't wrong to feel what he feels, but the film is smart enough to know he's wrong about her, and it never lets him (or us) off the hook for that. The nonlinear structure isn't just a gimmick, it mirrors exactly how memory actually works when you're picking apart a relationship after the fact — the good days bleeding into the bad ones out of order. Zooey Deschanel and Joseph Gordon-Levitt are so good at playing two people who are compatible in every way except the one that matters. The "expectations vs. reality" split-screen sequence is one of my favorite pieces of editing in any romantic film, and the ending earns its optimism without undoing anything the rest of the movie built. A perfect, quietly devastating little movie about the lies we tell ourselves when we're falling for someone.

texto: Você nunca quis ser a namorada de ninguém e agora é a esposa de alguém! Team Tom, eu não aceito discussões; eu sei que o Tom romantizou MUITO a Summer e criou na cabeça dele uma versão dela que provavelmente nunca existiu, mas também acho impossível assistir esse filme e não entender a frustração dele. O problema é que ele se apaixonou pela ideia de quem ela poderia ser, enquanto ela estava tentando deixar claro o que queria desde o começo. E o filme é muito inteligente em mostrar isso sem contar a história de um jeito completamente linear. A gente sente a esperança do Tom, depois vê tudo desmoronar e entende que algumas memórias ficam muito mais bonitas na nossa cabeça do que foram na realidade. Agora, o final eu gostei MUITO. Quando parece que finalmente acabou, ele conhece Autumn. E eu gosto disso porque não transforma o término em “tudo deu errado”. O Tom precisava passar por aquilo pra perceber que a vida continuava. Summer não era a vilã. Tom também não era um santo. Eram duas pessoas querendo coisas diferentes e tentando transformar isso em alguma coisa que funcionasse. Mas ainda sou Team Tom. Pode me julgar. E aquele “eu realmente espero que você seja feliz” no final? Depois de tudo? Eu teria ido embora pela janela, e o final com a Autumn? Depois de tudo que esse homem passou, eu só pensei: finalmente, Tom. Vai conversar com outra mulher e NÃO projeta uma vida inteira nela, pelo amor de Deus.
